what: DaVita runs about 2,700 dialysis clinics in the United States and abroad, treating patients whose kidneys have failed, usually three times a week for the rest of their lives.
customers: Patients with end-stage kidney disease, paid for by Medicare, Medicaid and commercial insurers.
money: clinics abroad and integrated kidney care
moat: A clinic within reach of patients who must attend three times a week, in a two-company industry where opening a competing clinic nearby rarely makes sense.
risks: About 90% of treatments are paid at government rates, which barely cover the cost; the profit comes from a small number of commercially insured patients
GLP-1 weight loss drugs may slow the growth of diabetic kidney disease over time
opportunities: 11.6 times earnings and 7.6 times free cash flow with $1.3B of free cash flow
Analysts see about 42% upside, with 7 covering the stock
Berkshire Hathaway has been a large holder, and the company buys back stock aggressively
watch: Treatment volume growth and the commercial insurance mix, which drives the profit.
